findings.title: immediateDelete branch cancels in SendGrid but leaves the DB row, and still uses the 100-slot cancel quota
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true the function POSTs a cancel to SendGrid and returns. It neither deletes the `workflowReminder` row nor sets `cancelled`. Two consequences follow. First, in the reschedule path in handleNewBooking the row survives with `scheduled=true` and a `referenceId` until the cron's generic cleanup removes it once `scheduledDate` has passed. Second, this branch is exactly the immediate cancellation that the PR says is limited to 100 pending cancellations. Every reschedule via handleNewBooking therefore still consumes a SendGrid cancel slot. Once the cap is hit, further cancels fail and the emails are sent anyway, which is the original bug. Either delete the row after cancelling, or use the lazy `cancelled=true` path wherever the row will survive (rescheduled bookings). Reserve immediate cancel for cases where the row is cascade-deleted, such as workflow or step deletion.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch and blocks later reminders on every run
findings.body: The whole loop is inside a single try/catch, and the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` calls are lazy Prisma promises that only execute at the final `Promise.all`. If one `client.request` throws (invalid or expired batch_id, rate limit, transient error), the loop exits. No row is deleted, including those already cancelled in SendGrid. The next cron run fetches the same rows in the same order and hits the same failing reminder first. That one bad row then stops every reminder after it from being cancelled, so those emails are still sent. Wrap each reminder in its own try/catch, and delete or mark each row right after its own successful cancel.

findings.title: Cancellations made shortly before the send time can still result in the email going out
findings.body: The cancellation is deferred to a cron run every 15 minutes and only covers reminders with `scheduledDate` within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled when the reminder is due in, say, 5–15 minutes, the row is only flagged `cancelled`. The next cron run may come after the send time, or after the cutoff SendGrid allows for cancelling a scheduled send. The email is then sent for a cancelled booking. The earlier step at line 34 also deletes any row whose `scheduledDate` has passed, so the cancel flag is lost. The PR claims to fix the problem, but this window is left open. Cancelling immediately when the reminder is due within about the next hour (the pending-cancel cap is the problem for far-future sends, not near ones) would close it.

findings.title: `client` (@sendgrid/client) is used in the cron but its API key is never set in this file
findings.body: Only `sgMail.setApiKey` is called here. `@sendgrid/mail` keeps its own client instance, whereas the default export of `@sendgrid/client` is a separate singleton. Elsewhere `client.setApiKey` is called in emailReminderManager.ts, but that module is not imported by this API route. The new cancel loop now depends on `client.request` for `/v3/user/scheduled_sends`. If the singleton has no key in this process, every cancel fails with 401. The surrounding try/catch swallows that with a console.log, and nothing is cancelled. Call `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` in this file.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation (now DB-write based) is fire-and-forget instead of awaited
findings.body: Previously the `workflowReminder.deleteMany` calls were included in the awaited `Promise.all`. Now `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called without `await` or collection. The DB update (`cancelled=true`) and the row delete happen only inside these floating promises. In a serverless runtime the invocation can be frozen or terminated once the response is returned, and unhandled work is not guaranteed to finish. If the write is lost, the reminder is never flagged, the cron never cancels it, and the email or SMS is sent for a cancelled booking. The same unawaited pattern is used in `requestReschedule` in bookings.tsx and in handleNewBooking. Collect these promises and await them with the other promises.

findings.title: try/catch around unawaited async calls can never catch anything
findings.body: The `forEach` callbacks call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without awaiting them. These functions are async and catch their own errors, so the surrounding try/catch with `log.error("Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders")` is dead code. The cancellations also run un-awaited, so the reschedule can proceed (and the request can finish) before they complete. Await them with `Promise.all` if the error handling is meant to be real.

findings.title: `Prisma` is now an unused value import
findings.body: The import was changed from `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` to a value import that also pulls in `Prisma`. After removing the `Prisma.BatchPayload` usage, `Prisma` is no longer referenced anywhere in the file, so it will trigger an unused-import lint warning. The same edit left a missing trailing comma. In the commented-out `testAction` block the diff also strips indentation, which is pure noise.

findings.title: No tests for the new deferred-cancellation flow
findings.body: The PR changes the cancellation contract: `cancelled` flag, lazy vs. immediate delete, and the cron cancelling reminders within the next hour. It adds no tests. Nothing covers `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (null referenceId, immediateDelete, lazy flag) or the cron's selection and cancel logic. Nothing covers the failure mode that motivated the PR, where more than 100 cancellations are pending. These paths are easy to regress and hard to verify manually.
